title: CHAPTER EIGHT. On the ceremonial law: definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): By this law God's Church in ye Old Testament stood as governed as an infant and a girl under elemental mysteries (Gal. 4:1-3; Heb. 8:5; 10:1; Col. 2:14, 11). — After ye moral law follows ye CEREMONIAL, which stands as an ordinance belonging toward God containing precepts concerning ye external worship belonging toward God toward be observed in ye Old Testament Church, for signifying, prefiguring, and sealing ye promised good, and for preserving ye sworn order in ecclesiastical assemblies and actions. — CHAPTER EIGHT. On ye ceremonial law.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER EIGHT. On the ceremonial law.

After the moral law follows the CEREMONIAL, which is an ordinance of God containing precepts concerning the external worship of God to be observed in the Old Testament Church, for signifying, prefiguring, and sealing the promised good, and for preserving the sworn order in ecclesiastical assemblies and actions.
By this law God's Church in the Old Testament was governed as an infant and a girl under elemental mysteries (Gal. 4:1-3; Heb. 8:5; 10:1; Col. 2:14, 11).
source_text: CAPUT OCTAVUM. De lege cerimoniali. Haec de lege morali: Sequitur CERIMONIALIS, quae est ordinatio Dei continens praecepta de cultu Dei externo in Ecclesia V.T. observanda ad significandum, praefigurandum & obsignandum bonum promissum, & ad iuratas in conventibus & actionibus Ecclesiasticis conservandum. Hac lege Ecclesia Dei in V.T. ut infans & puella sub elementis mysteriis gubernata fuit. Vide Gal. 4:1-3; Heb. 8:5; 10:1; Col. 2:14, 11.
